project.title: European Design Festival
project.format: Festival identity system spanning posters, banners, and flags

why: A strong poster-system reference for translating civic urgency into event graphics: the work uses protest rhetoric, hand-drawn declarations, and European-flag fragments to make a design festival feel argumentative rather than merely celebratory.

compositions.title: Declarative slogan posters
compositions.study: Statements such as 'Reset to default settings,' 'Make bold statements,' and 'Who draws the line?' are treated as the image itself, giving each poster a blunt verbal hook before any secondary explanation appears.
compositions.reuse: Let a short declarative line occupy the hero position when a poster needs immediate ideological clarity and can rely on typography more than illustration.

compositions.title: European-flag fragments as modular fields
compositions.study: The graphics borrow parts of European flags instead of quoting one nation wholesale, turning familiar stripes and color blocks into a shared but unstable political backdrop.
compositions.reuse: Sample recognizable civic symbols in fragments when a poster should feel public and collective without collapsing into one literal emblem.

compositions.title: Cross-format protest system
compositions.study: The same rough lettering and confrontational statements carry across posters, banners, and flags, so the identity reads like a coordinated demonstration rather than isolated layouts.
compositions.reuse: Build one loud graphic grammar that can survive format changes when an event identity needs street-level cohesion across print surfaces.

assets.notes: Bold hand-drawn lettering makes the posters feel urgent and human instead of polished or institutional.
assets.reuse: Use imperfect lettering when a poster should signal debate, dissent, or participation rather than corporate neutrality.

assets.role: shared political color and shape system
assets.notes: European-flag elements create a modular palette and geometry that ties the festival to a continental conversation without relying on one badge-like logo lockup.
assets.reuse: Base poster color systems on extracted civic fragments when an event spans multiple countries or publics.

assets.notes: The slogans borrow professional design terminology while also referring to the financial crisis, giving the posters both insider wit and public relevance.
assets.reuse: Write copy that carries two readable meanings when a poster must speak to a field audience and a broader social context at once.

implementation.format: Poster-led event identity with supporting banner and flag applications
implementation.notes: The official Studio Dumbar case study provides enough evidence to keep this as an accepted poster reference: event context, strategic framing, explicit visual ingredients, and multiple poster applications are all documented on the source page.
